question: Does an assistant-authored structural claim about treatment-effect ordering improve prediction of genuine randomized job-training effects over equally trained conventional causal estimators, without reusing Sachs data or pretending to observe individual counterfactuals?
candidate_prior: GPT-derived qualitative prior, explicitly UNVERIFIED: in historical NSW job training, individuals with both 1974 AND 1975 recorded earnings equal to zero have non-smaller average training effects on 1978 earnings than participants with any positive earnings. This is a speculative structural inequality, not a fact established by donor weights or causal data.

source.name: National Supported Work Demonstration (NSW) randomized 1970s job training experiment, Dehejia-Wahba subsample
source.primary: LaLonde 1986, Evaluating the Econometric Evaluations of Training Programs with Experimental Data
source.secondary: Cunningham Causal Inference: The Mixtape, causaldata::nsw_mixtape; NBER nswre74 treated/control
source.expected_schema: 11 columns data_id,treat,age,educ,black,hisp,marr,nodegree,re74,re75,re78, optionally Rdatasets first metadata column rownames (not a feature). All expected column names case-sensitive. No mirrors or alternative controls. Data must be finite; unique data_id.
source.information_contamination: Historically published extensively and plausible GPT pretraining exposure. Not original external first use, no new randomized participants.

protocol.outcome: re78, annual earnings in historical dollars; not individual potential outcome
protocol.treatment: treat binary randomized assignment 1 versus 0. All original 445 experimental records only; no PSID/CPS observational comparators.
excluded_features: any group identifier other than data_id for deterministic splitting
protocol.effect_group: U=1 when re74==0 and re75==0, else U=0. No special cases based on heldout group outcome.
protocol.split: Per treatment assignment separately sort individuals by SHA256 UTF8('GKD07-fold-v1|'+data_id); take treated FIT first 111, VALID next37, DEV last37; controls FIT first156, VALID next52, DEV last52. 267 FIT,89 VALID,89 DEV; no source numerical outcome used in splitting.
protocol.propensity: Known experimental assignment fraction p=185/445, held constant in FIT/VALID/DEV.
protocol.pseudo_outcome: For each VALID/DEV individual, Z = treat*re78/p - (1-treat)*re78/(1-p). Randomization gives E[Z|pretreatment covariates] = conditional treatment effect under assignment exchangeability; individual Z is NOT individual counterfactual.
protocol.candidate_estimator: FIT-only within-U subgroup difference in treated and control re78 means. Impose donor U effect >= non-U effect via weighted isotonic pooling: if subgroup U effect < non-U, pool both to FIT pooled group effects weighted by subgroup FIT counts; otherwise retain subgroup effects. No tuning.
strong_controls: FIT-only pooled randomized difference in means, constant for all DEV participants
FIT-only unconstrained two-U-group randomized difference-in-means; same data and 2 groups

FIT-only fully fitted ridge S-learner with intercept, treat, U, treat*U, log1p(re74), log1p(re75), treat*log1p(re74), treat*log1p(re75); ridge penalty alpha=1 on all nonintercept columns in outcome units / 10000, same features for treatment 0/1; effect is pred(T=1)-pred(T=0)
Reverse monotonic sham imposes effect_U <= effect_nonU on same FIT-only subgroup estimates
Same donor prior conventional deterministic implementation, intended exact equal-information tie (no claim independent algorithm)
protocol.baseline_selection: Select strongest of pooled, unconstrained, fully fitted ridge by minimum squared error on 89 VALID individuals using their pseudo-outcomes. Fixed control order breaks ties. Candidate donor and sham do not influence selection. No training on validation outcomes.
protocol.primary_score: Mean square error across 89 DEV pseudo-outcomes, reported as RMSE in historical dollars, compared with frozen VALID-selected strongest conventional. Relative RMSE gain = 1 - donor_rmse / best_conventional_rmse.
protocol.uncertainty: Exactly 2000 paired bootstrap resamples of 89 DEV participant indices with fixed xorshift32 seed 7007; calculate paired relative RMSE gain and the nearest-rank 2.5% and 97.5% percentiles. This is exploratory because single small historical cohort.
protocol.stratum_diagnostics: Report separate DEV RMSE on U=1 and U=0 and on two predeclared DEV subgroups: first and second half by the sorted SHA256(data_id) order. No primary threshold respecification.
protocol.signal: PUBLIC_DEV_SIGNAL only if >=5% donor RMSE gain against VALID-selected best conventional, >=5% gain against reverse-monotone sham, bootstrap lower 2.5 percentile gain >0, and donor nonregressing in each DEV half. Otherwise PUBLIC_DEV_NO_GO.
protocol.scientific_pass: ALWAYS FALSE: historically reused public trial, GPT prior may recall dataset, small 89-person DEV, no multiple independent RCT replications, no native learner adaptation or actual new intervention action.
protocol.mismatch: SOURCE_NO_GO if pinned original CSV has wrong fields, row counts, treatment balance, missing or nonfinite values, duplicate data_id, empty treatment subgroup; stop before DEV score and never silently substitute a different source.

contrasts: Distinct from GKD-06 same-cell protein conditional prediction: this is a real historical randomized treatment effect; distinct from existing Yggdrasil source-free closed-loop mechanisms; no duplicate prior NSW experiment found in PR search.
